title: Traditional Mysore Pak
summary: A traditional South Indian melt-in-mouth sweet made with roasted gram flour (besan), sugar syrup at one-string consistency, and warm clarified butter (ghee).

ingredients_or_materials.name: Pure Desi Ghee (ತುಪ್ಪ)
ingredients_or_materials.note: Kept warm and melted on low heat in a side pan

ingredients_or_materials.name: Water
ingredients_or_materials.note: Just enough to dissolve the sugar

tools: Small sauce pan (for keeping ghee hot)

steps.instruction: Sieve the gram flour twice into a mixing bowl to prevent lumps, then mix with 1/4 cup of warm ghee to form a smooth paste.
steps.spoken_tip: Mixing a little warm ghee directly into the flour before adding it to syrup prevents lumps from forming.

steps.instruction: In a heavy-bottomed kadai, add sugar and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a boil until one-string consistency (oru kambi padam) is reached.
steps.spoken_tip: Check the syrup between your thumb and index finger; it should stretch into a single delicate thread.

steps.instruction: Lower the flame and slowly pour the gram flour paste into the bubbling syrup while stirring continuously without stopping.
steps.spoken_tip: Stir vigorously in one direction so no dry pockets remain.

steps.instruction: Gradually ladle in hot melted ghee, one ladle at a time, allowing the mixture to completely absorb each ladle before adding the next.
steps.spoken_tip: The ghee must be hot when added, otherwise the mixture will cool down and turn rubbery.

steps.instruction: When the mixture starts frothing, turns honeycomb-like, and leaves the sides of the pan cleanly, immediately transfer it to the greased tray.
steps.spoken_tip: Do not pat it down flat or press it; let the natural bubbles stay inside for that porous texture.

steps.instruction: Let it cool for 10 minutes until warm, then slice gently into diamond or rectangular pieces with a greased knife.
steps.spoken_tip: Cut while it is still warm; if it sets completely, it will crumble when sliced.

tips: Keep the ghee continuously hot on a low flame on an adjacent burner.
Do not compress or press the hot mixture after pouring into the tin; natural pores give Mysore Pak its classic texture.
safety_notes: Hot sugar syrup and boiling ghee reach very high temperatures; beware of splatters when ladling hot ghee.
Use a deep, heavy pan and long-handled wooden spoon to protect your hands.
